_notes: Side works (DESIGN §8.8): the thing a priest does besides the parish, taken on for years, costing hours every week, reaching milestones, and finishing — or not. One at a time; the hours come off the same week as everything else.

works.label: Write a book
works.blurb: Two hundred pages on the one thing you actually know about, at four hours a week, for about four years. A publisher in Indiana might take it.

milestones.line: The book has a shape: four chapters drafted and the argument of the fifth on an envelope.
A publisher in Indiana has read sixty pages and wants the rest by Advent, which is not possible and will happen anyway.

done.line: The book is out. Three hundred copies to seminaries, a review in a journal eleven people read, and a box of them in the rectory hall that will still be there when you are moved.

risk.line: The manuscript is finished and nobody wants it. Two presses say no kindly and one does not answer, and it sits in the drawer under the engineer's report.

works.label: An hour a week on the radio
works.blurb: The diocesan station wants somebody who can talk for an hour without notes and not be dull. Sunday evenings, live, with telephone calls.

milestones.line: The Sunday hour has regulars: a woman from Waukegan who telephones every week, and a man who disagrees with you professionally.
A station two dioceses over has picked up the hour, which nobody at the chancery knew was possible.

done.line: Three years of Sunday evenings. People you have never met know your voice, stop you in car parks in other counties, and tell you what you said in 2016.

risk.line: The station drops the hour after a caller asks about something and you answer honestly. Nobody says that is why.

works.label: A lecture series around the diocese
works.blurb: Six evenings, six parish halls, the same six talks, four hundred miles a term. Somebody has to explain this stuff to grown adults.

milestones.line: The series has outgrown the halls it was booked into, and two pastors have asked for it in Lent.

done.line: Two years of evenings, about nine hundred people, and a diocese where a surprising number of laypeople can now tell you what the Church actually teaches about the thing they were angry about.

works.label: Translate something nobody has translated
works.blurb: A fourteenth-century text nobody has put into English, at three hours a week, with a Latin dictionary from the seminary you were not supposed to keep.

milestones.line: Book one is done and is bad, and you begin it again knowing what the man actually sounds like.
A scholar in Louvain has written to say that your reading of a passage in book three is wrong, at length, with warmth.

done.line: Five years. A university press takes it. It will be the standard English text for forty years and be read by perhaps two thousand people, all of whom needed it.

effects.key: translated a text nobody else would

works.label: Lead a parish pilgrimage
works.blurb: Forty-one parishioners, a coach, an airline, the Holy Land or Rome, and a year of Tuesday evenings arranging it.

milestones.line: Forty-one are signed up, two have died since signing, and the deposit is paid.

done.line: Eleven days. Mass on Calvary at six in the morning with forty-one people from one parish, and a man of sixty who had not been to confession since his divorce asking you in the hotel corridor.

effects.value: travelled:eleven days in the Holy Land

risk.line: The trip is cancelled six weeks out by something nobody controls, the deposits take a year to come back, and two families blame the parish.

works.label: The county jail, Thursday mornings
works.blurb: Forty minutes out, a locker for your keys, a room with a table, and men who have nobody else coming. No stipend, no notice from anybody.

milestones.line: Eleven men come to the Thursday room now, and one of them has asked to be baptized.
A man you saw for two years is out, and is at the eight o'clock on Sunday, at the back, in a jacket that does not fit.

done.line: Four years of Thursdays. Nobody in the diocese knows you do this except the chaplain's office and about two hundred men, some of whom write.

effects.key: went to the jail on Thursdays

works.label: A seat on the hospital board
works.blurb: The Catholic hospital wants a priest at the table who can read a balance sheet and will say the awkward thing about the ethical directives.

milestones.line: You have read four hundred pages of board papers and stopped one thing that should have been stopped.

done.line: Three years at that table. The chaplaincy is funded, the directives held in a merger, and every senior person in that building takes your telephone call.

works.label: Preach retreats for other parishes
works.blurb: Three or four a year, somebody else's people, a weekend at a time, and a stipend the parish does not see.

milestones.line: Four parishes have had you now and two have asked for you again, which is the whole test.

done.line: Three years of other men's parishes. Eleven pastors owe you a weekend, a great many people have heard the six talks, and you know exactly which of the six is the one that does the work.
